content: HOME > Articles > Articles of ICECH HUST 2025 > SOCIAL MEDIA INFLUENCERS AND GENERATION Z’S WILLINGNESS TO PARTICIPATE IN THE CIRCULAR ECONOMY: THE MODERATING ROLE OF PERCEIVED GREENWASH ICECH.HUST.2025.88 SOCIAL MEDIA INFLUENCERS AND GENERATION Z’S WILLINGNESS TO PARTICIPATE IN THE CIRCULAR ECONOMY: THE MODERATING ROLE OF PERCEIVED GREENWASH Research purpose: Grounded in the Stimulus Organism Response (SOR) framework, Persuasion theory, and Inspiration theory, this study examines how social media influencers (SMIs) shape Generation Z’s willingness to participate in the Circular Economy (CE). A moderated serial mediation model is developed in which inspiration and awareness function as sequential mediators, while perceived greenwash (GW) moderates both direct and indirect effects of SMIs on CE participation. Research motivation: As environmental concerns intensify, the CE has become a central approach to reducing waste and promoting sustainable consumption. At the same time, SMIs have emerged as powerful agents of influence, shaping pro-environmental behaviors among digital-native audiences. However, the growing phenomenon of greenwashing, when sustainability claims lack authenticity, poses a serious threat to influencer credibility. Yet, little is known about how perceived GW alters the persuasive process linking SMIs’ influence to CE-oriented engagement, especially in emerging economies such as Vietnam. Research design, approach, and method: A quantitative survey was conducted with 414 valid responses from Generation Z participants in Ho Chi Minh City. The questionnaire measured perceived influencer impact, inspiration, awareness, perceived GW, and CE willingness. Data were analysed using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modelling (PLS SEM) with 5,000 bootstrap resamples to test the moderated serial mediation framework. Main findings: Results reveal that SMIs enhance willingness to participate in CE through a sequential process of inspiration leading to greater awareness. However, when followers perceive high levels of greenwashing, these indirect effects weaken significantly, indicating that GW diminishes both the inspirational appeal and the awareness-raising capacity of influencers. This finding highlights perceived authenticity as a critical condition for translating digital influence into sustainable action. Practical/managerial implications: The study underscores that authentic, transparent, and evidence-based influencer communication can effectively motivate CE participation among young consumers. Brands should avoid symbolic or misleading sustainability claims that trigger greenwashing perceptions, while policymakers and educators can leverage credible influencers to normalize circular practices and nurture long term pro-environmental mind set. ban-sao-cua-mar32-completed-full-paper-submit-after-conference-1885-20251112-094152

title: EXPLORING THE IMPACT OF ANTHROPOMORPHISM ON PARASOCIAL RELATIONSHIP WITH VIRTUAL INFLUENCERS: THE MEDIATING ROLE OF TRUSTWORTHINESS AND WISHFUL IDENTIFICATION - ICECH2026
content: HOME > Articles > Articles of ICECH HUST 2025 > EXPLORING THE IMPACT OF ANTHROPOMORPHISM ON PARASOCIAL RELATIONSHIP WITH VIRTUAL INFLUENCERS: THE MEDIATING ROLE OF TRUSTWORTHINESS AND WISHFUL IDENTIFICATION ICECH.HUST.2025.87 EXPLORING THE IMPACT OF ANTHROPOMORPHISM ON PARASOCIAL RELATIONSHIP WITH VIRTUAL INFLUENCERS: THE MEDIATING ROLE OF TRUSTWORTHINESS AND WISHFUL IDENTIFICATION Research purpose: This research explores how anthropomorphism influences the parasocial relationships that Generation Z in Ho Chi Minh City develop with virtual influencers, highlighting the mediating effects of trustworthiness and wishful identification. Research motivation: Although virtual influencers are experiencing rapid growth, academic research in this area remains limited compared to the extensive body of work on human influencers. Previous studies predominantly investigated individual mediating mechanisms in isolation. This study seeks to address this gap by simultaneously examining perceived trustworthiness and wishful identification, thereby providing a more comprehensive understanding of the psychological processes underlying consumer relationships with virtual influencers. Research design, approach, and method: A quantitative survey was conducted with Gen Z respondents who had prior exposure to virtual influencers. Data were collected via online and direct questionnaires and analyzed using Structural Equation Modeling (SEM) with SmartPLS and SPSS software. Main findings: The results show that anthropomorphic features of virtual influencers positively influence both trustworthiness and wishful identification. Both factors significantly mediate the relationship between anthropomorphism and parasocial relationships, with wishful identification exerting a stronger mediating effect than trustworthiness. Practical implications: Marketers should focus on designing virtual influencers that evoke wishful identification, as this more strongly shapes consumer relationships than trustworthiness. Campaigns should target the predominantly female Gen Z audience on platforms such as TikTok and Instagram, while ensuring a balance between personality and transparency to foster both emotional engagement and long-term brand loyalty. ban-sao-cua-mar31-final-completed-1832-20251021-202536

title: EXPLORING CONSUMER INTENTION AND BEHAVIOR TOWARD ENERGY SAVING PRODUCTS: A BIBLIOMETRIC ANALYSIS OF SCOPUS PUBLICATIONS - ICECH2026
content: HOME > Articles > Articles of ICECH HUST 2025 > EXPLORING CONSUMER INTENTION AND BEHAVIOR TOWARD ENERGY SAVING PRODUCTS: A BIBLIOMETRIC ANALYSIS OF SCOPUS PUBLICATIONS ICECH.HUST.2025.33 EXPLORING CONSUMER INTENTION AND BEHAVIOR TOWARD ENERGY SAVING PRODUCTS: A BIBLIOMETRIC ANALYSIS OF SCOPUS PUBLICATIONS The growing urgency of sustainable consumption has stimulated increasing scholarly attention to consumer intentions toward energy-saving products. Understanding the intellectual development, geographical patterns, and thematic evolution of this research domain is essential for advancing both academic and policy agendas. The objective of this study is to provide a systematic bibliometric overview of publications on consumer intentions to adopt energy-saving products, with particular emphasis on growth trajectories, influential sources, collaboration structures, and emerging conceptual directions. The analysis is based on 147 documents published between 1985 and 2024, retrieved from the Scopus database. Bibliometric techniques, including descriptive performance analysis, citation analysis, co-authorship mapping, and keyword co-occurrence analysis, were employed using VOSviewer to explore the intellectual, social, and conceptual structures of the field. The results indicate two distinct phases of development: a formative period (1985 – 2011) with limited scholarly activity and a transformative period (2012 – 2024) marked by rapid growth, averaging over ten publications per year. Keyword analysis reveals a conceptual shift from technical efficiency and environmental concerns toward behavioral frameworks, including the Theory of Planned Behavior, and more recently, organizational and systemic contexts such as households, university staff, and the circular economy. esg14-toan-vu-le-exploring-consumer-intention-and-behavior-toward1

title: GREEN AND SUSTAINABLE ENTREPRENEURIAL INTENTIONS: EXPLORING RESEARCH FROM THE SCOPUS DATABASE THROUGH BIBLIOMETRIC ANALYSIS - ICECH2026
content: HOME > Articles > Articles of ICECH HUST 2025 > GREEN AND SUSTAINABLE ENTREPRENEURIAL INTENTIONS: EXPLORING RESEARCH FROM THE SCOPUS DATABASE THROUGH BIBLIOMETRIC ANALYSIS ICECH.HUST.2025.34 GREEN AND SUSTAINABLE ENTREPRENEURIAL INTENTIONS: EXPLORING RESEARCH FROM THE SCOPUS DATABASE THROUGH BIBLIOMETRIC ANALYSIS Amid escalating environmental pressures, green and sustainable entrepreneurship has gained prominence as a pathway to reconcile growth with the Sustainable Development Goals. Based on the Scopus database, this study employs bibliometric methods to clarify the developmental trends of the topic, “green and sustainable entrepreneurial intentions,” drawing on 236 published articles. The results indicate that China leads in terms of the number of publications, followed by Southeast Asian countries such as Malaysia, Indonesia, and India. The educational context is the focus of most studies, which indicate a shift from analyzing entrepreneurial intentions to examining actual entrepreneurial behavior. Co-authorship analysis indicates that research groups have not established strong long-term connections; rather, small and relatively new groups have made substantial contributions to the overall understanding of the field. Literature converges around six main themes: (1) Education and the Development of Sustainable Entrepreneurial Intentions, (2) Green entrepreneurship in educational contexts, (3) Environmental performance and green corporate governance, (4) Green innovation and entrepreneurial intentions, (5) Personal motivation and behavioral perceptions, and (6) Theoretical foundations in green entrepreneurship research. The number of publications has risen sharply since the COVID-19 pandemic, reflecting the increasingly evident link between global crises and sustainable entrepreneurship. This study not only systematizes a comprehensive overview of green and sustainable entrepreneurial intentions but also outlines future research. esg16-final-completed-1341-20251009-134302

title: LEGAL FRAMEWORK PROMOTING SUSTAINABLE DEVELOPMENT IN VIETNAM’S COMMERCIAL BANKS - ICECH2026
content: HOME > Articles > Articles of ICECH HUST 2025 > LEGAL FRAMEWORK PROMOTING SUSTAINABLE DEVELOPMENT IN VIETNAM’S COMMERCIAL BANKS ICECH.HUST.2025.36 LEGAL FRAMEWORK PROMOTING SUSTAINABLE DEVELOPMENT IN VIETNAM’S COMMERCIAL BANKS Research purpose: This paper critically reviews Vietnam’s evolving legal framework for sustainable development in commercial banking, examining how primary statutes and SBV instruments translate sustainability objectives into governance, risk, and disclosure practice, and how they align with international standards. Research motivation: As Vietnamese banks face simultaneous domestic mandates and global market expectations, a clear view of legal strengths, gaps, and convergence pathways is needed to support credible implementation and investor confidence. Research design, approach, and method: The study adopts a qualitative, theory-informed approach grounded in stakeholder, legitimacy, and institutional theories. Guided by these perspectives, it synthesizes core legal and policy instruments and benchmarks Vietnam’s direction of travel against widely recognized international reference points. A structured set of comparative dimensions is applied to organize evidence on scope, governance, process discipline, risk integration, disclosure architecture, and implementation. Main findings: Vietnam shows substantial progress toward a coherent, enforceable framework that aligns sustainability objectives with banking practice. The analysis indicates broad convergence with international expectations alongside features tailored to domestic priorities. At the same time, the framework would benefit from clearer common definitions, more consistent market-facing disclosures, stronger links between engagement evidence and risk decisions, and continued capacity development to support practical implementation. Practical implications: In light of the identified gaps, actions should be sequenced and audience-specific. Policymakers should first strengthen the legal foundations and the shared data environment, so that definitions are clear and information flows are reliable. Regulators should then convert those foundations into consistent supervisory tools, including standardized templates, reporting formats, and proportionate guidance, all of which support implementation without creating duplicative burdens. Practitioners should in turn embed the resulting requirements into governance, credit processes, and internal controls, ensuring that disclosures reflect real risk decisions rather than after-the-fact narratives. esg18-final-completed-1487-20251012-020611

title: THE IMPACT OF FIRMS’ CLIMATE RISK ON FIRM VALUE: THE MODERATING ROLE OF ESG AND A MACHINE LEARNING APPROACH - ICECH2026
content: HOME > Articles > Articles of ICECH HUST 2025 > THE IMPACT OF FIRMS’ CLIMATE RISK ON FIRM VALUE: THE MODERATING ROLE OF ESG AND A MACHINE LEARNING APPROACH ICECH.HUST.2025.37 THE IMPACT OF FIRMS’ CLIMATE RISK ON FIRM VALUE: THE MODERATING ROLE OF ESG AND A MACHINE LEARNING APPROACH Research purpose: This study investigates the effect of firms’ climate risk on firm value and examines whether ESG practices moderate this relationship in emerging and frontier markets. Research motivation: Climate risk has become a critical concern for firms in vulnerable economies where exposure to extreme weather events is high, but insurance mechanisms and safeguards remain limited. Although prior studies link climate risk to firm value, evidence remains fragmented and concentrated in developed markets, creating a need for more context-specific research. Research design, approach, and method: We analyze 1,683 firm-year observations from 561 firms across Vietnam, India, the Philippines, South Africa, and Malaysia during 2022–2024. To estimate causal effects, we adopt a Double Machine Learning (DML) framework that integrates Random Forest and XGBoost, allowing us to account for nonlinearity and control for confounding bias. Main findings: The results show that climate risk significantly reduces firm value, and this negative impact is amplified when interacted with ESG scores. These findings highlight the potential double-edged role of ESG in high-risk environments. Practical/managerial implications: Our results emphasize the importance of embedding ESG practices into firms’ financial strategies and technological innovation efforts. Moreover, they call for stronger regulatory frameworks and policy support to improve market resilience to climate-related risks. esg19-completed-full-paper-submit-after-conference-1924-20251115-225628

title: EXPLORING THE APPLICATION OF THE THEORY OF PLANNED BEHAVIOR TO EXPLAIN UNIVERSITY STUDENTS' ENERGY-SAVING INTENTIONS AND BEHAVIORS: A SYNTHESIS OF CO-KEYWORD AND CONTENT ANALYSIS OF PUBLICATIONS RETRIEVED FROM SCOPUS - ICECH2026
content: HOME > Articles > Articles of ICECH HUST 2025 > EXPLORING THE APPLICATION OF THE THEORY OF PLANNED BEHAVIOR TO EXPLAIN UNIVERSITY STUDENTS’ ENERGY-SAVING INTENTIONS AND BEHAVIORS: A SYNTHESIS OF CO-KEYWORD AND CONTENT ANALYSIS OF PUBLICATIONS RETRIEVED FROM SCOPUS ICECH.HUST.2025.38 EXPLORING THE APPLICATION OF THE THEORY OF PLANNED BEHAVIOR TO EXPLAIN UNIVERSITY STUDENTS’ ENERGY-SAVING INTENTIONS AND BEHAVIORS: A SYNTHESIS OF CO-KEYWORD AND CONTENT ANALYSIS OF PUBLICATIONS RETRIEVED FROM SCOPUS Energy conservation has emerged as a fundamental component of sustainability transitions, with universities serving a dual function as significant energy consumers and crucial environments for fostering pro-environmental behavior in future leaders. The Theory of Planned Behavior (TPB) has been extensively utilized to examine university students’ goals regarding energy conservation; nonetheless, current research is disjointed concerning geographical coverage, methodological frameworks, and theoretical advancements. This study combines bibliometric analysis with content analysis to thoroughly investigate the intellectual and methodological framework of TPB applications in this field. A systematic search of the Scopus database identified 98 qualifying papers, 28 of which directly utilized the TPB. Bibliometric co-keyword analysis emphasized the central role of TPB and Structural Equation Modeling (SEM) in explaining behavioral intentions. Results also showed that energy-saving behavioral tendencies were related to environmental awareness, concern about global warming, and pro-environmental attitudes. Meanwhile, content analysis of 24 full-text reports was found to indicate the role of key variables of TPB in research contexts in different countries. The results of content analysis continued to emphasize the key role of the SEM method. Moreover, the TPB has often been augmented with additional latent variables to improve the explanatory power of the research model. Five groups of additional variables were found, including (1) social norms and influence, (2) personal cognition and perceived control, (3) environmental cognition and affect, (4) policy and external support, and (5) individual or behavioral factors. Research indicates that enhancing the TPB’s impact on students’ energy-saving behavioral intentions necessitates expanded geographical scope, methodological variety, and comprehensive assessment of model extensions. esg25-final-completed-1195-20251006-214256

title: SUSTAINABLE DEVELOPMENT GOALS AND FINANCIAL PERFORMANCE OF COMMERCIAL BANKS IN VIETNAM - ICECH2026
content: HOME > Articles > Articles of ICECH HUST 2025 > SUSTAINABLE DEVELOPMENT GOALS AND FINANCIAL PERFORMANCE OF COMMERCIAL BANKS IN VIETNAM ICECH.HUST.2025.39 SUSTAINABLE DEVELOPMENT GOALS AND FINANCIAL PERFORMANCE OF COMMERCIAL BANKS IN VIETNAM Research purpose: Our study aims to examine the sustainability and enduring effectiveness of the implementation of Sustainable Development Goals within the banking sector, in order to determine if it indeed enhances and contributes to greater financial performance in comparison to the conventional organizational practices that were previously employed. Research motivation: Sustainable development constitutes an imperative necessity and an inevitable trend within the developmental process of every nation globally, encompassing Vietnam. Consequently, both commercial banks and governmental bodies have been actively engaged in fostering high-profit activities while simultaneously striving to achieve the specific sustainable development goals and contribute to the advancement of the domestic market economy and facilitating integration into the international market. Research design, approach, and method: We collect both macroeconomics and bank-specific data for the period spanning from 2008-2022. We utilize 3 variables to represent the impact of sustainable development goals on banks’ financial performance, specifically SDG3, SDG6, and SDG8. We employ the Generalized Method of Moments (GMM) technique to overcome the endogeneity problem. Main findings: Applying the GMM method, our findings show that the correlation between the attainment of sustainable development goals and the financial performance of commercial banks does exist, specifically: SDG3, SDG6, and SDG8. The results show that advancements in these sustainable development goals may enhance banks’ financial performance. Practical/managerial implications: Banks should develop green financial products, such as preferential lending options for renewable energy projects and enhancements in sustainable infrastructure. Concurrently, the utilization of digital technologies to optimize lending operations and manage environmental hazards will significantly enhance financial performance. fin3-final-completed-878-20250926-132035

title: DIGITAL TRANSFORMATION IN VIETNAMESE COMMERCIAL BANKS CURRENT SITUATION AND FUTURE RESEARCH DIRECTIONS - ICECH2026
content: HOME > Articles > Articles of ICECH HUST 2025 > DIGITAL TRANSFORMATION IN VIETNAMESE COMMERCIAL BANKS CURRENT SITUATION AND FUTURE RESEARCH DIRECTIONS ICECH.HUST.2025.41 DIGITAL TRANSFORMATION IN VIETNAMESE COMMERCIAL BANKS CURRENT SITUATION AND FUTURE RESEARCH DIRECTIONS Research purpose: In the current era of digital technological development, the traditional business model of commercial banks is being replaced by a modern one. Especially after the COVID-19 pandemic, the majority of people’s tendency to use digital services has prompted banks to actively engage in the digital transformation process. In Vietnam, despite making progress in applying digital technology to banking operations, digital transformation has confronted numerous challenges. This article aims to explore the strategic challenges that commercial banks have encountered in their digitalization process to enhance operational efficiency and customer satisfaction, achieving sustainable growth in the digital era. By identifying challenges in banking digitalization, this paper also proposes several comprehensive solutions to promote this process, to create a modern, flexible, and sustainable banking system. Research motivation: In Vietnam, the digitalization of the banking sector is recognized as one of eight priority areas under Prime Minister’s Decision No. 749/QD-TTg (2020), which approves the “National Digital Transformation Program to 2025, with an Orientation to 2030.” In recent years, the banking industry in Vietnam has undergone the most rapid and significant digital transformation. The article examines problems surrounding banking digitalization, providing strategic solutions to help Vietnamese commercial banks alleviate existing barriers and enhance long-term competitiveness. Research design, approach, and method: This study applied a narrative review approach to examine the challenges and potential solutions to the digital adoption process in the banking sector. The criteria for selecting documents are determined as follows: (1) publications from 2020 onwards to reflect recent trends in digital banking, fintech, and legal regulations; (2) sources focused on the Vietnamese context or similar emerging markets; (3) research documents on aspects of technology application, digital infrastructure, cybersecurity, human resources, customer satisfaction, and legal frameworks. Main findings: The study emphasized that digital transformation is crucial for enhancing customer satisfaction, keeping pace with state-of-the-art technologies, and promoting sustainable development goals. Recognizing the urgency of this issue, Vietnamese commercial banks are proactively advancing their digital transformation, reaching the second of three levels in banking digitalization. After evaluating the current situation, the article identified several challenges that Vietnamese banks have encountered during their digitalization process. One of the primary challenges is the lack of a comprehensive regulatory framework governing digital banking activities. Cybersecurity is another factor due to an increase in fraud cases, cyberattacks, and data breaches in the banking infrastructure. In addition, a shortage of well-qualified human resources remains a major challenge in the digitalization process of commercial banks, particularly experts in artificial intelligence, cybersecurity, and digital innovation management. Practical/Managerial implications: The proposed practical implications include establishing a comprehensive legal framework for digital banking, enhancing technology infrastructure and skilled human capital, and strengthening communicative strategies, as well as raising customer awareness regarding digital services and cybersecurity practices. The paper also provided a clear roadmap to accelerate banking digitalization in Vietnam in favour of sustainable development and long-term economic growth. fin5-final-completed-1337-20251009-130848

title: THE IMPACTS OF LIQUIDITY ON FIRM EFFICIENCY AND PROFITABILITY: EVIDENCE FROM VIETNAMESE LISTED FIRMS - ICECH2026
content: HOME > Articles > Articles of ICECH HUST 2025 > THE IMPACTS OF LIQUIDITY ON FIRM EFFICIENCY AND PROFITABILITY: EVIDENCE FROM VIETNAMESE LISTED FIRMS ICECH.HUST.2025.43 THE IMPACTS OF LIQUIDITY ON FIRM EFFICIENCY AND PROFITABILITY: EVIDENCE FROM VIETNAMESE LISTED FIRMS Research purpose: This study examines the impact of corporate liquidity on profitability and operational efficiency using a panel dataset of the 100 largest non-financial firms listed on the Ho Chi Minh City Stock Exchange (HoSE) over the period 2014–2023. Research motivation: The relationship between liquidity, profitability, and efficiency remains inconclusive in prior studies, particularly in emerging economies. Vietnam’s dynamic but volatile market provides a unique setting to re-examine this linkage, thereby, offering empirical evidence and practical insights for optimizing liquidity management under macroeconomic uncertainty Research design, approach, and method: Panel regression techniques-specifically OLS, Fixed Effects, and Random Effects models-are employed in this study, drawing upon the Trade-off, Pecking Order, Signaling, and X-Efficiency theories. Liquidity is measured by current ratio (CR) and quick ratio (QR). Firm performance is measured by ROA, ROE, NPM and ATR. Main findings: While liquidity enhances profitability (ROA, ROE, NPM), it hinders operational efficiency (ATR), representing the costs of idle cash. Leverage has a detrimental impact on profitability while firm size diminishes asset efficiency of assets most likely due to increasingly complex operations. Practical/managerial implications: The management of liquidity is essential to enhance profitability, but too much cash may limit efficiency. This research contributes to the literature not only with data from a dynamic transition economy, but it can also help practitioners make informed decisions when operating in the highly volatile environment of an emerging market. fin7-final-completed-1080-20251004-175741

title: THE INFLUENCE OF FEMALE CEOS ON CAPITAL STRUCTURE AND FIRM PERFORMANCE OF LISTED FIRMS IN VIETNAM - ICECH2026
content: HOME > Articles > Articles of ICECH HUST 2025 > THE INFLUENCE OF FEMALE CEOS ON CAPITAL STRUCTURE AND FIRM PERFORMANCE OF LISTED FIRMS IN VIETNAM ICECH.HUST.2025.44 THE INFLUENCE OF FEMALE CEOS ON CAPITAL STRUCTURE AND FIRM PERFORMANCE OF LISTED FIRMS IN VIETNAM Research purpose: The aim of the research is to explore female chief executive officers’ (CEOs) effects on capital structure and firm performance in Vietnam, which is a unique context shaped by gender roles and economic transition. Research motivation: While overseas scholarship suggests that female-led firms exhibit lower risk- taking, stronger governance compliance, and potentially enhanced performance, little is known about how these dynamics are enacted in Vietnam, a transitioning, export-led economy with deeply embedded cultural tradition. This paper fills this gap by sharing empirical evidence of Vietnam’s listed firms. Research design, approach, and method: The research utilises panel data from eighty-six of the firms that have been listed in Vietnam through Vietstock in the period 2020 to 2024. We used regression modelling to evaluate potential relationships between firm level female leadership and the outcomes of Return on Assets (ROA), capital structure and liquidity. Our selected control variables were firm size, firm age, industry, board size, board independence, profitability, and ownership structure. Main findings: Empirical evidence demonstrates that female CEOs influences financial performance positively, namely increasing ROA and liquidity, and using more conservative capital structures with lower leverage usage. The findings highlight the critical role of gender diversity in executive leadership, positioning female CEOs as key catalysts for sustainable growth and resilience in Vietnam’s corporate landscape, setting a foundation for further exploration and policy development. Practical/managerial implications: These findings suggest that gender diversity among senior executives enhances profitability and financial performance, underlining women as a strategic leader asset. To policymakers, the findings reinforce policies favoring women in leadership positions; to corporations, it focuses attention on the capacity of women CEOs to drive growth through savvy financial stewardship. ban-sao-cua-fin8-final-completed-959-20250930-221146

title: EQUITY MARKET TIMING AND RESILIENT FINANCE: RETHINKING CAPITAL STRUCTURE IN DISRUPTIVE ECONOMIES - ICECH2026
content: HOME > Articles > Articles of ICECH HUST 2025 > EQUITY MARKET TIMING AND RESILIENT FINANCE: RETHINKING CAPITAL STRUCTURE IN DISRUPTIVE ECONOMIES ICECH.HUST.2025.45 EQUITY MARKET TIMING AND RESILIENT FINANCE: RETHINKING CAPITAL STRUCTURE IN DISRUPTIVE ECONOMIES Research purpose: This paper systematically reviews the equity market timing hypothesis to evaluate its impact on capital structure and, more critically, on a firm’s long term financial resilience Research motivation: Capital structure remains one of the most contested questions in corporate finance. Traditional theories cannot fully explain why firms issue overvalued equity or repurchase undervalued shares. Market timing offers a behavioral perspective, but its long-term persistence and implications for resilience remain underexplored, especially in emerging markets. Research design, approach, and method: This study adopts a conceptual synthesis methodology. It systematically reviews foundational and contemporary scholarship, synthesizes cross-country evidence, and contextualizes equity market timing within disruptive and emerging economic environments by integrating theoretical and empirical insights. Main findings: Evidence indicates that equity market timing significantly affects short-term capital structures, but its persistence is context-dependent. Effects are short-lived in developed markets as firms revert to target leverage, but are stronger and longer-lasting in emerging markets due to higher informational inefficiencies. The analysis highlights market timing as a tactical tool that interacts with institutional frameworks and managerial behavior. Practical/managerial implications: For managers, market timing presents opportunities to lower financing costs and enhance shareholder value but also carries risks of mispricing and dilution. Policymakers should strengthen disclosure standards and investor protections to mitigate opportunistic behavior while supporting firms’ resilience. ban-sao-cua-fin11-final-completed-992-20251002-020659

title: THE DYNAMICS OF DISRUPTION: A TOE MODEL FROM ENVIRONMENTAL PRESSURE TO MANAGERIAL COMPETENCIES IN BANKING SECTOR - ICECH2026
content: HOME > Articles > Articles of ICECH HUST 2025 > THE DYNAMICS OF DISRUPTION: A TOE MODEL FROM ENVIRONMENTAL PRESSURE TO MANAGERIAL COMPETENCIES IN BANKING SECTOR ICECH.HUST.2025.26 THE DYNAMICS OF DISRUPTION: A TOE MODEL FROM ENVIRONMENTAL PRESSURE TO MANAGERIAL COMPETENCIES IN BANKING SECTOR Research purpose: This study proposes and validates a cross-level theoretical model, transposing the Technology-Organization-Environment (TOE) framework to explain the pathway from macro-level environmental pressures to the formation of micro-level managerial competencies required to lead digital transformation in Vietnam’s banking sector. Research motivation: While the Vietnamese banking sector faces an urgent mandate for digital transformation, failure rates remain high. This is not a technological paradox but a strategic one, stemming from a critical knowledge gap: the “black box” mechanism through which macro-level environmental dynamics are translated into a targeted, micro-level managerial competency strategy. This study addresses this gap. Research design, approach, and method: This study employs a rigorous, two-stage systematic literature review (SLR) adhering to PRISMA 2020 guidelines. An initial inductive search on the Scopus database identified emergent contextual drivers, which were subsequently validated and structured through a second, deductive search against the established constructs of the TOE framework. Main findings: This study makes two primary theoretical contributions. First, it finds that environmental pressures from competitors, government, and customers interact to create an “Environmental Pressure Spiral,” a reinforcing feedback system that acts as the primary catalyst for the digital transformation imperative. Second, this process is mediated by a “Competency-Technology Feedback Loop,” a co-evolutionary mechanism between human capital and technological assets. These dynamics drive the need for a hierarchical competency set, where a foundational Digital Mindset enables the acquisition of Digital Knowledge and the application of Digital Skills. Practical/managerial implications: This study provides a diagnostic model for banking executives to translate environmental pressures into a competency development roadmap for leading effective digital transformation. It guides how to build a management team capable of navigating disruption by understanding how external pressures inform the need for specific digital mindsets, knowledge, and skills. ban-sao-cua-eco33-completed-full-paper-submit-after-conference-1856-20251108-093155

title: GREEN FINANCE RESEARCH TRENDS IN THE GREEN TRANSITION CONTEXT: A BIOGRAPHY ANALYSIS OF SCOPUS DATA (2015-2024) - ICECH2026
content: HOME > Articles > Articles of ICECH HUST 2025 > GREEN FINANCE RESEARCH TRENDS IN THE GREEN TRANSITION CONTEXT: A BIOGRAPHY ANALYSIS OF SCOPUS DATA (2015-2024) ICECH.HUST.2025.25 GREEN FINANCE RESEARCH TRENDS IN THE GREEN TRANSITION CONTEXT: A BIOGRAPHY ANALYSIS OF SCOPUS DATA (2015-2024) The green transition has emerged as a global strategic imperative, positioning green finance as a central mechanism for channelling capital into environmentally sustainable initiatives. Instruments that promote green finance encompass green bonds, green credits, and green investments, among others. These instruments not only direct capital toward environmentally friendly activities but also bring financial benefits to firms and enterprises. This study offers an exhaustive overview of the subject based on a bibliometric analysis of 128 papers indexed in Scopus from 2015 to 2024. The result illustrates a remarkable increase in literature publications since 2021, with China leading in both productivity and scholarly impact. Energy Economics is the most influential journal, with the high-impact publication being, “Can the green credit policy stimulate green innovation in heavily polluting enterprises?” Evidence from a quasi-natural experiment in China” by Hu, G.; Wang, X.; and Wang, Y. Keywords with high occurrence, which represent the core themes of the topic, include “green finance”, “green innovation”, “financial constraint”, and “green credit policy”. From the clustering of keywords, four primary research streams are identified: (i) foundations of green finance, (ii) policy implications, (iii) effects of green credit, and (iv) China’s green financial pathways. Future research should further examine the role of green credit in advancing green transformation, strengthening environmental regulation, fostering green innovation, and alleviating financial constraints. While the study provides valuable insights, its scope is constrained by reliance on the Scopus database, English-language sources, and an emphasis on development trends considered through the lens of the green transition. ban-sao-cua-eco32-final-completed-1416-20251010-151530

title: CARBON EMISSION REDUCTION IN THE CONTEXT OF GREEN TRANSITION: A BIBLIOGRAPHIC ANALYSIS OF STUDIES FOR THE PERIOD 2020-2024 - ICECH2026
content: HOME > Articles > Articles of ICECH HUST 2025 > CARBON EMISSION REDUCTION IN THE CONTEXT OF GREEN TRANSITION: A BIBLIOGRAPHIC ANALYSIS OF STUDIES FOR THE PERIOD 2020-2024 ICECH.HUST.2025.23 CARBON EMISSION REDUCTION IN THE CONTEXT OF GREEN TRANSITION: A BIBLIOGRAPHIC ANALYSIS OF STUDIES FOR THE PERIOD 2020-2024 As climate change intensifies, reducing carbon dioxide (CO₂) emissions has become a central pillar of sustainable development and global climate action. Countries around the world, such as China, Germany, and India, are adopting green transition policies encompassing renewable energy, green finance, and industrial restructuring. While existing studies have explored various aspects of green transition and carbon mitigation in specific fields, such as green finance, industrial restructuring, and sector-specific approaches, there is a lack of comprehensive analysis connecting these diverse domains globally. This study aims to bridge this gap by conducting a bibliometric analysis using data from the Scopus database. Bibliometric methods have been extensively applied in research areas like education, entrepreneurship, and social media, offering insights into publication patterns, collaboration networks, and thematic development. By applying bibliometric analysis to the topic of carbon dioxide emissions reduction in the context of green transition, this study identifies key research trends, influential authors and journals, and emerging topics that shape the landscape of carbon mitigation efforts worldwide. The findings provide a broad overview of the interdisciplinary connections among technology, economy, and policy, and they are beneficial to stakeholders and policymakers striving to achieve carbon neutrality and sustainable development goals. ban-sao-cua-eco29-final-completed-1411-20251010-151034

title: OPTIMIZED GA-LIGHTGBM MODEL FOR FORECASTING STOCK RETURN VOLATILITY OF SAO MAI GROUP (ASM.VN) IN THE SUSTAINABLE ENERGY SECTOR - ICECH2026
content: HOME > Articles > Articles of ICECH HUST 2025 > OPTIMIZED GA-LIGHTGBM MODEL FOR FORECASTING STOCK RETURN VOLATILITY OF SAO MAI GROUP (ASM.VN) IN THE SUSTAINABLE ENERGY SECTOR ICECH.HUST.2025.22 OPTIMIZED GA-LIGHTGBM MODEL FOR FORECASTING STOCK RETURN VOLATILITY OF SAO MAI GROUP (ASM.VN) IN THE SUSTAINABLE ENERGY SECTOR This study proposes a Genetic Algorithm–optimized LightGBM (GA – LightGBM) model for forecasting stock volatility of ASM.VN, demonstrating superior performance compared with traditional models (GARCH, SVMRegressor, XGBoost) and deep learning architectures (GRU, TabNet, Transformer, CNN, LSTM). The model achieves MAE = 0.0470; RMSE = 0.0731; R² = 0.8480; STD = 0.1480, with a mean R² = 0.805 across 5-fold cross-validation, indicating high accuracy and stability. Predicted volatility over 06 February 2025 – 06 March 2025 ranges from 0.1419 to 0.2154, reflecting moderate adjustment risk. SHAP analysis identifies key original features in descending order: HV, BB – width, BB – lower, VWAP, ATR, MA_21, BB – upper, OBV, highlighting the roles of market fluctuations, price amplitude, liquidity, and medium-term trends in shaping forecasts. Sensitivity analysis indicates colsample – bytree and num – leaves exert the strongest influence (ΔR² = 2.02% and 0.81%, respectively), whereas other hyperparameters produce minor variations (<0.6%), confirming model robustness. During the period starting 09 April 2025, US retaliatory tariffs (+46%) triggered strong volatility spikes in energy stocks, particularly ASM.VN (+130%), HDG.VN (+93%), BCG.VN (+60%), with differentiated forecasts persisting through September 2025. The GA – LightGBM model demonstrates strong potential for guiding investment strategies, risk management, and policy-sensitive market analysis. While empirical results are robust, economic implications emphasize practical benefits including risk-adjusted returns, improved hedging efficiency, and reduced pricing errors in derivative markets. Caution is warranted under “black swan” events or structural market changes, necessitating periodic retraining and hyperparameter monitoring to maintain predictive reliability. ban-sao-cua-eco28-completed-full-paper-submit-after-conference-1929-20251116-013426

title: FACTORS INFLUENCING THE ADOPTION OF GREEN LOGISTICS IN MANUFACTURING ENTERPRISES: A PLS-SEM APPROACH FROM THAI NGUYEN PROVINCE - ICECH2026
content: HOME > Articles > Articles of ICECH HUST 2025 > FACTORS INFLUENCING THE ADOPTION OF GREEN LOGISTICS IN MANUFACTURING ENTERPRISES: A PLS-SEM APPROACH FROM THAI NGUYEN PROVINCE ICECH.HUST.2025.21 FACTORS INFLUENCING THE ADOPTION OF GREEN LOGISTICS IN MANUFACTURING ENTERPRISES: A PLS-SEM APPROACH FROM THAI NGUYEN PROVINCE Green logistics plays a pivotal role in advancing sustainable supply chains, yet its uptake in emerging economies remains uneven. This study explores the determinants of green logistics adoption among manufacturing enterprises in Thai Nguyen province, Vietnam, a growing industrial hub with strong foreign investment and increasing sustainability commitments. Drawing upon the Theory of Planned Behavior (TPB) and the Technology – Organization – Environment (TOE) framework, the research model tests the effects of environmental–social awareness (ENV), external pressure (EXT), cost-effectiveness perception (ECO), internal capabilities (INT), and technological infrastructure (TEC) on the adoption of green logistics (USE). Survey data were collected from 30 enterprises (60 valid responses) and analyzed using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM). The results indicate that ENV, ECO, EXT, and TEC exert significant positive impacts on USE, while INT shows no significant effect. Moreover, EXT also indirectly affects USE through ENV, highlighting a partial mediation mechanism. The model explains 63.8% of the variance in green logistics adoption, demonstrating substantial explanatory power. These findings theoretically validate the integration of TPB and TOE in a provincial manufacturing context, while practically suggesting that raising environmental awareness, enhancing perceptions of cost-effectiveness, strengthening technological infrastructure, and leveraging institutional pressures are crucial levers to accelerate green logistics adoption in emerging economies. ban-sao-cua-eco25-final-completed-1331-20251009-085827

title: IMPACT OF CEO CHARACTERISTICS ON THE PERFORMANCE OF LISTED COMPANIES IN VIETNAM - ICECH2026
content: HOME > Articles > Articles of ICECH HUST 2025 > IMPACT OF CEO CHARACTERISTICS ON THE PERFORMANCE OF LISTED COMPANIES IN VIETNAM ICECH.HUST.2025.46 IMPACT OF CEO CHARACTERISTICS ON THE PERFORMANCE OF LISTED COMPANIES IN VIETNAM Abstract This study investigates how CEO characteristics influence firm performance in the context of Vietnam, an emerging market. The dataset comprises 30 publicly listed companies on the Ho Chi Minh City Stock Exchange (HOSE) over the period 2010–2023. The Ordinary Least Squares (OLS) and quantile regression methods are employed as the primary estimation technique. The findings indicate that CEO age and tenure, have a statistically significant and positive impact on firm performance when measured by Return on Assets (ROA) as well as Return on Equity (ROE), underscoring the importance of managerial experience and qualifications in enhancing shareholder value. Conversely, CEO ownership is found to be negatively associated with ROE, suggesting that concentrated control may reduce governance efficiency, potentially due to weakened oversight or entrenchment effects. Research purpose: This study aims to empirically examine the effects of various CEO characteristics—including age, tenure, duality, educational background, gender, and ownership stake—on the financial performance of publicly listed companies in Vietnam, specifically those in the VN30 index. The research intends to uncover both average and distributional impacts of these CEO traits on firm profitability, measured by ROA and ROE, to provide a nuanced understanding of leadership influence in an emerging market context. Research motivation: The motivation stems from the growing recognition that CEOs’ personal attributes significantly shape firms’ strategic directions and outcomes, yet empirical evidence in emerging markets like Vietnam remains sparse. Prior research has predominantly focused on developed economies, leaving a gap concerning how CEO characteristics manifest impacts under the dynamic and evolving corporate governance environment of Vietnam’s stock market. Addressing this gap offers important insights for both academia and practitioners navigating leadership selection and corporate governance in transitional economies. Research design, approach, and method: This study adopts a quantitative research design using a panel dataset of 30 VN30 companies listed on the Ho Chi Minh City Stock Exchange over the period 2010 to 2023. The empirical analysis applies two main econometric methods: Pooled Ordinary Least Squares (OLS) regression to estimate the average effects of CEO characteristics on firm performance indicators (ROA and ROE), and Quantile Regression to explore heterogeneous impacts across different levels of financial performance. CEO characteristics examined include duality, age, gender, educational background, ownership, and tenure, while firm-level control variables account for size and age. This combination of methods allows for a comprehensive assessment of both mean and distributional relationships between leadership traits and corporate outcomes. Main findings: The findings demonstrate that CEO age and tenure possess strong, positive, and statistically significant impacts on firm performance indicators ROA and ROE, confirming the critical role of experience and leadership stability in enhancing profitability. CEO duality is found to positively influence ROA, especially in high-performing firms, while CEO ownership shows a negative association with ROE, indicating governance risks associated with concentrated control. Educational background and gender reveal mixed effects, highlighting contextual nuances in Vietnam’s corporate landscape. The quantile regression results emphasize heterogeneity, with CEO characteristics impacting firms differently depending on their performance strata. Practical/managerial implications: These results suggest that firms should carefully consider CEO experience and tenure in succession planning and leadership development to foster sustainable financial performance. The positive role of duality in asset efficiency calls for balancing centralized authority with adequate governance safeguards to optimize decision-making. Moreover, the negative implications of concentrated CEO ownership underscore the need for strengthened supervisory mechanisms. The nuanced effects of education and gender imply that supplementary managerial training and inclusive policies could further enhance leadership effectiveness in Vietnam’s evolving market environment. ban-sao-cua-fin12-final-completed-1477-20251012-000533

title: DETERMINANTS OF EMPLOYEE GREEN BEHAVIOR IN HEALTHCARE SECTOR: EVIDENCE FROM FACILITIES IN HANOISECTOR: EVIDENCE FROM FACILITIES IN HANOI - ICECH2026
content: HOME > Articles > Articles of ICECH HUST 2025 > DETERMINANTS OF EMPLOYEE GREEN BEHAVIOR IN HEALTHCARE SECTOR: EVIDENCE FROM FACILITIES IN HANOISECTOR: EVIDENCE FROM FACILITIES IN HANOI ICECH.HUST.2025.29 DETERMINANTS OF EMPLOYEE GREEN BEHAVIOR IN HEALTHCARE SECTOR: EVIDENCE FROM FACILITIES IN HANOISECTOR: EVIDENCE FROM FACILITIES IN HANOI Research purpose: The purpose of this research is to explore the determinants of employee green behavior in the healthcare sector, with a focus on the roles of environmental knowledge (EK), environmental attitude (EA), and green human resource management (GHRM). Both in-role and extra-role green behaviors are analyzed to to gain a broad perspective on how employees engage in environmentally responsible practices in the workplace. Research motivation: While the healthcare sector is a significant contributor to environmental impacts, Although healthcare services generate considerable environmental impacts, studies on employees’ eco-friendly practices within this sector remain scarce, especially in the Vietnamese context. This study addresses this gap by exploring how individual-level and organizational-level factors jointly influence sustainable workplace practices. Research design, approach, and method: Drawing on the Theory of Planned Behavior and Social Exchange Theory, an integrated framework was proposed. Survey data from 203 healthcare employees in Hanoi using a structured questionnaire and analyzed using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM). Main findings: EA emerged as the most influential predictor of both in-role and extra-role green behaviors. EK influenced these behaviors through both direct and mediated pathways, with its effect being stronger when transmitted via EA. GHRM practices significantly promoted green behavior, particularly in in-role actions. Practical/managerial implications: The results emphasize the need for healthcare organizations to simultaneously strengthen employees’ environmental knowledge, foster positive environmental attitudes, and implement supportive GHRM practices. Such a dual focus on individual cognition and organizational systems can effectively cultivate a green culture within healthcare institutions. ban-sao-cua-esg1-final-completed-1827-20251021-113331

title: INNOVATION AND DISCOURAGED BORROWING AMONG SMES: EVIDENCE FROM ASIAN ECONOMIES - ICECH2026
content: HOME > Articles > Articles of ICECH HUST 2025 > INNOVATION AND DISCOURAGED BORROWING AMONG SMES: EVIDENCE FROM ASIAN ECONOMIES ICECH.HUST.2025.53 INNOVATION AND DISCOURAGED BORROWING AMONG SMES: EVIDENCE FROM ASIAN ECONOMIES Research purpose: This study examines how innovation influences borrowing behavior among small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) in 19 Asian countries, focusing on discouraged borrowing – when firms avoid applying for credit due to fear of rejection. Research motivation: Discouraged borrowing is a hidden form of financial exclusion that constrains SME growth. While widely studied in Europe and advanced economies, evidence for Asia remains limited despite distinct financial infrastructures and institutions. This study tests whether innovation reduces discouragement and whether firm size moderates this relationship Research design, approach, and method: Using pooled cross-sectional World Bank Enterprise Surveys (2013 – 2024) covering 12,000+ SMEs across 19 Asian economies, we estimate logistic regressions with extensive controls and country – industry – year fixed effects, include interaction terms for firm-size heterogeneity, and run robustness checks by income group and separately for product and process innovation. Main findings: Innovation intensity significantly reduces discouraged borrowing, supporting its role as a positive signal of competitiveness and growth potential. The effect varies across firm sizes – strongest for large firms – yet benefits are evident for SMEs overall. Robustness checks confirm consistency across upper- and lower-middle-income economies and show that both product and process innovation independently lower discouragement. Practical implications: Policies should strengthen innovation as a credible financing signal. Governments can expand innovation funds and credit guarantees to support smaller firms, while lenders tailor products for innovative SMEs. Because both product and process innovation reduce discouragement, support should span a broad range of innovation activities, alongside stronger credit information systems – especially in lower-middle-income countries – to promote financial inclusion. ban-sao-cua-fin28-final-completed-1162-20251006-161825

title: BRIDGING THE GAP IN VIETNAM'S SOCIAL HOUSING: AN ANALYSIS OF CURRENT STATUS AND DEVELOPMENT BARRIERS - ICECH2026
content: HOME > Articles > Articles of ICECH HUST 2025 > BRIDGING THE GAP IN VIETNAM’S SOCIAL HOUSING: AN ANALYSIS OF CURRENT STATUS AND DEVELOPMENT BARRIERS ICECH.HUST.2025.31 BRIDGING THE GAP IN VIETNAM’S SOCIAL HOUSING: AN ANALYSIS OF CURRENT STATUS AND DEVELOPMENT BARRIERS Research purpose: This study aims to assess the current status of social housing development in Vietnam, identify the key factors limiting the effectiveness of social housing provision, and propose viable policy solutions to enhance housing accessibility for low-income populations. Research motivation: Rapid urbanization and rising income inequality in Vietnam have worsened the shortage of affordable housing for low-income groups, especially in major cities. Despite government policies, significant gaps remain between social housing targets and actual delivery. This gap motivates the research to fill knowledge voids and support better policy planning. Research design, approach, and method: This study applies a mixed-methods approach using secondary data. Quantitative analysis of government and market data evaluates housing supply trends, while qualitative thematic analysis with NVivo following Braun and Clarke’s model identifies key challenges in social housing development. Main findings: The research shows Vietnam consistently falls short of its national social housing targets, with development focused mainly in urban centers while rural areas are underserved. Major barriers include limited land allocation, slow disbursement of financial support, unattractive profits for private developers, and poor integration with essential infrastructure. These challenges collectively hinder the pace and effectiveness of social housing delivery. Practical/managerial implications: To bridge the gap between policy and practice, Vietnam needs institutional reforms including a dedicated agency to streamline approvals and data management. Financial incentives such as higher profit ceilings, better credit guarantees, and expanded preferential loans can attract private investment and support demand. Integrating social housing development with targeted infrastructure will improve accessibility and appeal. Policies should also broaden eligibility to include informal workers and migrants, promoting greater social equity. Together, these measures can drive sustainable growth and enhance housing access for vulnerable populations. ban-sao-cua-esg7-completed-full-paper-submit-after-conference-1910-20251114-235854

title: CHALLENGES AND OPPORTUNITIES IN IMPLEMENTING ISO 20022 FOR INTERNATIONAL REMITTANCE: A CASE STUDY OF BIDV - ICECH2026
content: HOME > Articles > Articles of ICECH HUST 2025 > CHALLENGES AND OPPORTUNITIES IN IMPLEMENTING ISO 20022 FOR INTERNATIONAL REMITTANCE: A CASE STUDY OF BIDV ICECH.HUST.2025.57 CHALLENGES AND OPPORTUNITIES IN IMPLEMENTING ISO 20022 FOR INTERNATIONAL REMITTANCE: A CASE STUDY OF BIDV Research purpose: This study explores ISO 20022 adoption at BIDV, identifying key challenges and benefits, and proposes a strategic roadmap with practical guidelines to support other Vietnamese financial institutions in implementing similar modernization initiatives. Research motivation: SWIFT’s global adoption of ISO 20022 requires financial institutions to adapt. In Vietnam, banks like BIDV face challenges, including legacy systems and limited expertise, which lead to message rejections, data loss, and reconciliation issues. Yet, practical implementation research remains scarce, especially in developing economies undergoing similar remittance system transitions. Research design, approach, and method: This research employed a mixed-methods approach, comprising case studies, surveys, interviews, and SWOT analysis, guided by the Technology Acceptance Model (TAM) to assess user perceptions before and after the implementation of ISO 20022. BIDV ultimately selected the bridged translation model as the most feasible solution for a smooth system transition. Main findings: ISO 20022 adoption significantly improved operations at BIDV, enhancing message quality, efficiency, and compliance. Rejection rates fell from 9.2% to 1.4%, manual effort dropped 60%, and processing time decreased from 2.6 to 1.5 hours. Over 60,000 MX messages were processed, with 75% staff satisfaction in Q4 2023. Practical/Managerial Implications This thesis offers practical recommendations, highlighting phased implementation, cross-department coordination, and stakeholder training. It suggests permanent resource allocation, quarterly supervision, and proactive risk management to support sustained efficiency and ensure compliance in modernizing international remittance systems ban-sao-cua-fin35-final-completed-1699-20251015-112639

title: WHEN FEAR MEETS FINANCE: THE ROLE OF FOMO, FINANCIAL KNOWLEDGE, AND IMPULSIVENESS IN SHAPING FINANCIAL INVESTMENT DECISIONS AMONG VIETNAMESE UNIVERSITY STUDENTS - ICECH2026
content: HOME > Articles > Articles of ICECH HUST 2025 > WHEN FEAR MEETS FINANCE: THE ROLE OF FOMO, FINANCIAL KNOWLEDGE, AND IMPULSIVENESS IN SHAPING FINANCIAL INVESTMENT DECISIONS AMONG VIETNAMESE UNIVERSITY STUDENTS ICECH.HUST.2025.58 WHEN FEAR MEETS FINANCE: THE ROLE OF FOMO, FINANCIAL KNOWLEDGE, AND IMPULSIVENESS IN SHAPING FINANCIAL INVESTMENT DECISIONS AMONG VIETNAMESE UNIVERSITY STUDENTS Research purpose: The main purpose of this research is to examine the behavioral and cognitive factors that determine the personal financial investment behavior of Vietnamese university students. Specifically, the study focuses on three important psychological factors: Fear of Missing Out (FOMO), Financial Knowledge, and Impulsivity. While FOMO is the fear of missing out on opportunities, Financial Knowledge captures the cognitive ability to process financial information, and Impulsivity reflects the psychological tendency to act without careful consideration. In addition to these key factors, the study also examines the role of demographic characteristics such as age, gender, income, and field of study to determine whether they significantly influence students’ investment decisions. By analyzing these factors in combinationThe research aims to offer a thorough understanding of the investment practices employed by young and novice investors in the current context. Research motivation: The motivation behind this study stems from both practical and theoretical considerations. In recent years, Vietnam has experienced rapid economic growth and financial market expansion, leading to increased participation by individual investors, including university students. Young investors are often highly active on digital platforms and exposed to real-time financial information, making them susceptible to psychological factors such as FOMO. At the same time, students’ financial literacy remains relatively low, and impulsive behavior may further undermine rational decision-making. While behavioral finance research has extensively explored these factors in developed economies, it has paid limited attention to emerging markets, especially in Southeast Asia. Therefore, this study was motivated by the need to fill this gap and contribute to the behavioral finance literature by focusing on a sample of Vietnamese university students. Re search design, approach, and method: A quantitative research design was selected for this study. Data were gathered via a structured web-based questionnaire distributed in 2025. The survey targeted university students of different majors and years of study, resulting in 176 valid responses, targeting university students using purposive sampling. The questionnaire was designed using validated scales from previous studies: the financial literacy scale developed by Chen and Volpe (1998), the FOMO scale proposed by Przybylski et al. (2013), and the Barratt Impulsivity Scale (Barratt, 1965; Patton et al., 1995). Personal financial investment behavior was measured using items adapted from Johan Mattsson. Data were analyzed using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM), a powerful multivariate technique suitable for small to medium sample sizes and exploratory research settings. Main findings: The analysis revealed several key findings. First, FOMO was found to have a significant positive influence on students’ financial investment behavior, indicating that emotional pressure and the fear of missing opportunities drive students to participate in financial markets more actively. Second, financial knowledge showed a significant negative effect on investment behavior, suggesting that students with higher financial literacy tend to be more cautious and less likely to engage in risky or impulsive investment activities. This unexpected outcome may reflect the context of Vietnam, where awareness of financial risks discourages participation rather than encouraging it. Third, impulsiveness did not have a significant effect on investment behavior, which implies that young Vietnamese students may not act as rashly as expected in financial decisions, possibly due to limited resources and a cautious cultural approach. Finally, demographic factors such as gender, age, and income were not found to significantly influence investment behavior, highlighting that investment decisions in this age group are more strongly shaped by psychological and cognitive factors than by demographic characteristics. Overall, the model explains 12.1% of the variance in personal financial investment behavior. Practical/managerial implications: The findings of this study provide important implications for educators, policymakers, and financial institutions. From an educational perspective, the results underline the need for financial education programs that not only improve financial knowledge but also address psychological drivers of investment behavior, such as FOMO. For policymakers, the findings suggest that initiatives to promote financial literacy should be complemented by awareness campaigns on behavioral biases, enabling young investors to balance rational analysis with emotional control. For financial institutions, understanding the dual role of financial knowledge and emotional factors is crucial for designing investment products and advisory services tailored to young investors. Specifically, banks, securities firms, and fintech platforms should provide tools and educational resources that help students manage emotional impulses while making informed investment decisions. In the long run, strengthening the financial capability of students will not only improve individual welfare but also contribute to the sustainable development of Vietnam’s financial markets. ban-sao-cua-fin36-final-completed-1520-20251012-235313

title: A COMPREHENSIVE FRAMEWORK FOR EVALUATING UNIVERSITY ADMISSIONS COMMUNICATION ACTIVITIES IN VIETNAM - A RESEARCH MODEL PROPOSAL - ICECH2026
content: HOME > Articles > Articles of ICECH HUST 2025 > A COMPREHENSIVE FRAMEWORK FOR EVALUATING UNIVERSITY ADMISSIONS COMMUNICATION ACTIVITIES IN VIETNAM – A RESEARCH MODEL PROPOSAL ICECH.HUST.2025.28 A COMPREHENSIVE FRAMEWORK FOR EVALUATING UNIVERSITY ADMISSIONS COMMUNICATION ACTIVITIES IN VIETNAM – A RESEARCH MODEL PROPOSAL In Vietnam’s increasingly competitive higher education landscape, admissions communication is essential for institutional sustainability and growth. Yet, universities lack a systematic framework to evaluate its effectiveness. This study reviews existing literature and develops a comprehensive evaluation model tailored to the Vietnamese context. Research purpose: This study aims to propose and empirically validate a comprehensive model for evaluating admissions communication activities in Vietnamese universities by integrating theoretical foundations, prior studies, and pilot testing. Research motivation: Vietnamese universities face intense competition and often struggle to meet enrollment quotas. A systematic framework for evaluating communication effectiveness is lacking, hindering strategic optimization. This study aims to fill this gap. Research design, approach, and method: The study employs a mixed-method approach combining literature review, theoretical synthesis, and a pilot survey conducted at Hanoi University of Science and Technology (HUST). Measurement scales for five dimensions of communication effectiveness were developed and tested using reliability and validity analysis. Main findings: The study identifies five key evaluation dimensions: Information Quality and Relevance, Channel and Media Effectiveness, Stakeholder Engagement and Interaction, Brand Perception and Reputation, and Behavioral Outcomes and Enrollment Impact. Pilot testing with 183 respondents confirms strong reliability and construct validity of the proposed scales, providing empirical support for the conceptual model and hypotheses. Practical/managerial implications: The validated model and scales offer a practical framework for Vietnamese universities to systematically assess and enhance their admissions communication strategies. By applying the model, institutions can make evidence-based decisions on messaging, channel selection, and stakeholder engagement, thereby improving brand reputation and enrollment outcomes eco43-icech2025-revised-full

title: THE INTERRELATIONSHIP BETWEEN DIGITAL TRANSFORMATION AND GREEN TRANSITION IN THEORY AND PRACTICE IN VIETNAM’S ENTERPRISES - ICECH2026
content: HOME > Articles > Articles of ICECH HUST 2025 > THE INTERRELATIONSHIP BETWEEN DIGITAL TRANSFORMATION AND GREEN TRANSITION IN THEORY AND PRACTICE IN VIETNAM’S ENTERPRISES ICECH.HUST.2025.27 THE INTERRELATIONSHIP BETWEEN DIGITAL TRANSFORMATION AND GREEN TRANSITION IN THEORY AND PRACTICE IN VIETNAM’S ENTERPRISES In the context of global sustainable development, dual transformation combining digital transformation and green transition has become a strategic requirement for businesses. The study synthesizes documents, focuses on clarifying concepts related to dual transformation, including digital transformation and green transition, and analyzes the mutual relationship between digital transformation and green transition. The study emphasizes that digital transformation plays a catalyst role in promoting green efficiency, while green transition is the driving force for digitalization. In addition, the study also systematizes a number of theoretical frameworks, including TOE (Technology Organization-Environment), Institutional Theory, Resource Based View (RBV), and Dynamic Capabilities, to suggest a new theoretical framework for measuring and evaluating dual transformation. In addition, the study gathers initial successful results in the implementation of digital technology and green technology for energy management, emission reduction, transparent ESG reporting, and sustainable product development at three typical enterprises, including Vinamilk, Hoa Phat, and Vinfast. A limitation of this study is that it has not conducted quantitative or empirical analysis on a large data sample, so the level of statistical generalization is still limited.
